Extreme weather

The River Runs Dry

Zambia's Copperbelt mines draw power around the clock. The reservoir on the Zambezi starts full, but an El Niño drought is coming.

Play The River Runs Dry↗ Your decisions ↓

Choose your difficulty before you start. It’s free to play in your browser.

Location
Lusaka, Zambia
Starts in
2012
Your term
6 years

Your starting point

Your utility starts in 2012 with a hydro plant, a small diesel plant and a little solar. The dam supplies most of your electricity.

When inflow falls, each release uses water the river is slow to replace. The diesel plant is too small to take over when the reservoir runs low.

Learn how to play

Your decisions

  1. 01

    Use the time the reservoir buys you

    Watch the inflow forecast while the lake is still full. That's when you have time to build another source of power.

  2. 02

    Compare alternatives to hydro

    Check how much electricity a new plant would supply during a dry spell and what it would cost to run.

  3. 03

    Keep the mines supplied overnight

    Compare solar output with the industrial load. Work out what would keep the mines running between sunset and sunrise.

What would you build while the dam still has water?
